title: Rosh Hashanah: the symbolic foods
hookLine: pomegranate, dates, leeks and a fish head, each with a wish
tomorrow: the blessing over the shofar isn't for blowing it. so what is it for?

lines: MAKE A WISH BEFORE YOU BLOW.
cards: Birthday candles come with a rule: make a wish before you blow. Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish new year, has its own version, and it's on the plate. Apples dipped in honey.
A pomegranate split open. Dates, leeks, beets. And on some tables, a fish head looking up at everyone.
Each one comes with a wish, said out loud before the first bite, and the fish head is no exception.

teach.b: These are the simanim, the signs.

The Talmud's sage Abaye says that since signs carry meaning, a person should make a habit of eating, at the start of the year, gourd, fenugreek, leeks, beets and dates, foods that grow plentifully or taste sweet.
Later tables added more. The pomegranate, with the wish that our good deeds be as many as its seeds.

teach.h: THE HEAD, AND NOT THE TAIL.
teach.b: The fish head, for the line in Deuteronomy about being "the head, and not the tail." Apples in honey, for a sweet year.
Several of the wishes are puns: in Aramaic, the word for leek sounds like the word for cut off, so the wish is that whatever would harm us be cut off.
Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: a siman isn't a lucky charm.
It's a hope said out loud, and then eaten.
Each wish opens with the same words, may it be your will, which keeps the food a prayer and never a trick. That's the round, too.
Every line you've gathered these two weeks is a small siman: something set on the table of an ordinary day, standing for a bigger wish.

how: On the first nights of Rosh Hashanah, families eat apples dipped in honey and other simanim, such as pomegranate, dates, leeks, beets or a fish head, saying a short wish beginning "may it be your will" over each.

games.q: your roommate is hosting Rosh Hashanah dinner and can't find a pomegranate anywhere. she thinks the meal won't count. what does the tradition offer?
o: pick another food and say a wish with it; the list itself grew over time.
the meal doesn't count without the exact foods on the list.
skip the symbols entirely; only the prayers in synagogue matter.
games.why: Abaye's list was five foods; later tables added the pomegranate, the fish head and the apple. the heart of a siman is the wish.

practice: Take one simple food you have nearby: an apple slice, a date, a spoon of honey, a piece of bread. Before you eat it, say one wish for the year ahead, for yourself or for someone else.
Then taste it slowly, and let the wish go down with it.
